why: Connecting all points with the cheapest set of links and exactly one path between any two is a minimum spanning tree on the complete graph with Manhattan-distance weights. With n <= 1000 the dense O(n^2) Prim is the right tool.
hints: 'Exactly one simple path between any two points' describes a tree. Which tree are you after?
This is a minimum spanning tree. On a complete graph with up to 10^6 edges, Prim's algorithm with an array of 'cheapest link to the tree so far' beats sorting all edges for Kruskal.
dist[i] = cost to attach i; repeat n times: pick the unattached point with the smallest dist, add it to the answer, update dist for all others with the Manhattan distance. O(n^2) time, O(n) memory.
pitfalls: Building and sorting all n^2/2 edges for Kruskal works but is slow and memory-heavy in Python at n = 1000.
